summary: Tower constructed near Bayfield, WI by October 1934 to help protect the Apostle Islands; now listed as gone, with no staffing, fire or site record found.

facts.status_note: Listed as gone; the sources give no removal date
facts.agency: Wisconsin state conservation department, as named in a 1934 newspaper item

events.note: A newspaper item dated October 23, 1934 says a new fire tower had been constructed near Bayfield; no build date is given

evidence.supports: a new fire tower had been constructed near Bayfield
evidence.quote: a new fire tower constructed near Bayfield

evidence.supports: the Apostle Islands lie northeast of Bayfield
protecting the islands had been impossible for lack of equipment
evidence.quote: Active protection of them has been impossible heretofore due to lack of equipment

evidence.supports: the state conservation department announced the plan
evidence.quote: the state conservation department announced today

evidence.supports: the new tower and power boat had remedied the situation, per the department
a power boat suited to centrifugal pumps
evidence.quote: acquisition of a power boat suitable for centrifugal pumps

evidence.supports: forest protection of the islands to be extended the next spring
evidence.quote: Forest protection will be extended next spring to the Apostle Islands

evidence.supports: the county list marks the Bayfield tower as gone

sources.title: Bayfield (quoting the Oshkosh Daily Northwestern, October 23, 1934)

notes_for_editor: Rests on one 1934 newspaper item, quoted secondhand on the Forest Lookouts page, plus the county status listing. The original newspaper was not checked. The brief had no agency or height; the agency fact is the department named in that item. The Bayfield Heritage Association archive page and the Wisconsin Historical Society search for Bayfield County fire towers did not show this tower. Used one WebSearch call pair and about four page reads.
